audit.whatIsWrong: Early text had the right shape but no numbers, so 'poke him out' was advice without a lever.
audit.why: Orb of Deception is 970 to Razor Shuriken's 900, and his Q costs 75 energy at rank 1 with Shadow Slash at 290 range. Missed shurikens genuinely price him out of trading.
audit.corrected: Poke from 970 and make him spend energy answering; two whiffed Q's and he cannot trade at all.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 and first-item spikes never cited a cooldown, and phases[4].why / phases[5].why described Ahri spikes on rows the chart gives to Zed.
audit.why: Death Mark is 120/110/100s with a 3-second mark; Living Shadow is 20/19/18/17/16s and is his only escape. Those two timers are the entire mid-game.
audit.corrected: Spikes and phase whys rewritten around Death Mark's 120s and Living Shadow's 20s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Zed is untargetable while Death Mark dashes in; wants.you[1] actively told the reader to Charm the dash.
audit.why: Kit text: 'Zed becomes untargetable and dashes to an enemy champion, marking them.' A Charm or a full combo thrown at the approach hits nothing. The answer is spent on the landing.
audit.corrected: Hold Charm for the instant he becomes targetable again; keep one Spirit Rush charge to leave the 3-second mark's range.
sources: brief enemyKit R text and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] told the reader Zed 'roams off cross-map ults'.
audit.why: Death Mark is 625 range and single-target. Zed has no global or cross-map ultimate of any kind.
audit.corrected: He snowballs a lead into side-lane picks, not cross-map ultimates.

audit.whatIsWrong: LEVEL CHART DISAGREEMENT on rows 0, 4, 5 and 6: phases[].side reads Skill on all seven rows while win[] reads Ahri/Skill/Skill/Skill/Zed/Zed/Ahri.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the content layer, and the whys text describes exactly that shape (Ahri ahead at 1, Zed's level 6 and first item, Ahri late).
audit.corrected: phases[0].side Ahri, phases[4].side Zed, phases[5].side Zed, phases[6].side Ahri, ratings realigned.

edits.before: Spirit Rush online — three dashes change every rule: charm angles multiply and ganks stop working on you.
edits.after: Death Mark online — untargetable on the way in, three seconds of mark, and Charm is your only interrupt.

edits.before: Malignance spike: R cooldown drops and every dash window chains a full charm combo.
edits.after: His mark still wins the race — hold Charm for his landing, never for chip damage.

edits.before: Zed can't threaten a real all-in until he has Shadow-Q-E combo online with Death Mark, so early levels stay in your favor with Charm poke.
edits.after: Living Shadow is 20 seconds at rank 1 and Razor Shuriken costs 75 energy — poke him from 970 and he has no answer at all until Death Mark.

edits.before: Zed's Death Mark spike is one of the scariest all-in windows in mid lane — he can shadow-swap onto you, land Q-E, and detonate the mark for burst you can't out-trade without Charm ready.
edits.after: Death Mark makes him untargetable as he dashes in and then marks you for 3 seconds — never dump your combo into the approach, and charm him the instant he is targetable again.

edits.before: Zed still out-scales your early burst item because his mark damage scales with bonus AD and he only needs one clean engage to kill you before your combo finishes.
edits.after: His mark repeats a portion of everything he dealt during those 3 seconds, so one clean engage still kills you before your combo finishes — get the Zhonya's timing right.

edits.before: With a full combo and Spirit Rush available you out-range and out-reset him — Zed has to commit through vision to land Death Mark, and if he whiffs shadow he's dead to your burst.
edits.after: With a full combo and Spirit Rush you out-range and out-reset him — he has to commit through vision, and a charm landed as he swaps back to Living Shadow leaves him standing in your burst.

edits.before: Ahri's Orb of Deception poke and safer wave control outclass Zed before he has Death Mark online — he has no real answer to ranged harass at levels 1-2 beyond eating minion aggro to close distance, which costs him CS. Play aggressive with Charm punishes whenever he pushes to trade Qs, and bank mana for a level 2 all-in if he overextends. Zed players who rush the wave to level 6 fast are giving up tempo you should be capitalizing on right now.
edits.after: Orb of Deception reaches 970 against Razor Shuriken's 900, and Zed has no answer to ranged harass at levels 1-2 beyond eating minion aggro to close, which costs him CS. Punish with Charm whenever he steps up to trade Qs, and bank mana for a level 2 all-in if he overextends. His Q costs 75 energy at rank 1, so two missed shurikens leave him unable to trade at all — take that window while it is open.

edits.before: Both champions are fairly even through levels 3-5 in terms of raw poke — Zed's Q hurts but he's still without his ultimate, so neither side can force a kill outright. The moment he hits 6, though, the lane flips hard: Death Mark plus a shadow-swap dash means he can appear on top of you, combo, and mark for a burst window your Charm has to interrupt or you die. Save Charm specifically for this window and don't walk up to CS near his shadow range once he's 6 and you're not.
edits.after: Through 3-5 the poke is even — Razor Shuriken hurts but with no ultimate he cannot force anything, and Shadow Slash only reaches 290. At 6 the lane flips: Death Mark makes him untargetable through the dash in, so a Charm or combo spent on his approach hits nothing at all. Hold it for the moment he lands. Living Shadow is 20 seconds at rank 1 and it is his only way out, so if he spends it to poke, the twenty seconds behind it belong to you.

edits.before: Once you've got a full combo item and Spirit Rush charges available, you out-scale his all-in — Zed still one-shots squishies but he has to actually close the gap through your Charm, and if it lands mid-shadow-dash he's stuck and dead. Group for objectives and force him to engage into vision rather than pick him off; a fed Zed can still delete you in one rotation, so respect his all-in range even late and don't get caught alone in a side lane.
edits.after: With a full item and Spirit Rush charges you out-scale his all-in — Zed still one-shots squishies, but he has to close through your Charm, and a charm landed as he swaps back to Living Shadow leaves him stranded. Remember the untargetable dash: your burst waits for the landing, never the approach. Group for objectives, make him engage into vision, and never sit alone in a side lane on a 100-second ultimate.

edits.after: Hold Charm from level 6 onward for the moment Death Mark lands, not the dash in

edits.before: Zed wins by landing Death Mark, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Zed wins by arriving untargetable through Death Mark, marking you for three seconds, and repeating the damage before you can leave.

edits.before: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget R Spirit Rush (last dash) for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — he is untargetable through the dash, so your answer is spent AFTER he lands, never on the approach. - Living Shadow is 20s at rank 1 and his only escape; if he pokes with it, the next twenty seconds belong to you.

edits.before: Carry through picks — a landed charm is a won fight, and your dashes manufacture charm angles no one wards against.
edits.after: Carry through picks — charm him as he swaps back to Living Shadow and the assassin is stranded inside your team.

edits.before: If Zed takes first blood, tighten up: Death Mark is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q clears and stay relevant through charm picks.
edits.after: If Zed takes first blood, treat Death Mark as always up and never leave tower without Charm. A second kill means the duel is over — farm with Q, buy Zhonya's, and stay relevant through charm picks.

edits.before: Ahead, hunt the map: shove with Q, dash-flank every river, and charm-pick Zed's teammates until the lane lead is a game lead.
edits.after: Ahead, deny the reset: shove with Q, dash-flank other lanes, and come back to charm him whenever Living Shadow is on cooldown.

edits.before: The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: He is untargetable through the Death Mark dash — spend Charm on the landing, not on an approach that eats it.

edits.before: Q through his last-hit so both hits land, W if he eats the return, and walk — repeat until the charm window is lethal instead of optimistic.
edits.after: One dash held back carries you out of the three-second mark, and the repeat damage lands on the ground you already left.

edits.before: Zed whiffs Death Mark and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Razor Shuriken costs 75 energy — make him pay to answer you.

edits.before: That is Zed’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: A spent charm is twelve seconds of standing still with his mark on you.

edits.before: The last dash is your life insurance — an Ahri who spends all three going in is an assassin's favorite story.
edits.after: The last dash is what carries you out of the mark — an Ahri with no charges left just waits for it to pop.

edits.before: Charming on cooldown for chip damage and then facing his real engage with nothing — the charm is the matchup, not the poke.
edits.after: Past river with Charm down, Living Shadow gives him an angle from any bush and the mark starts before you see him.

edits.before: Track Zed’s Death Mark: The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Death Mark (120s at rank 1): untargetable on the way in, then a three-second mark repeating his damage. Charm the landing.

notes: Two hard errors: wants.you[1] instructed the reader to Charm the Death Mark dash, which is untargetable, and wants.foe[2] gave Zed 'cross-map ults' when Death Mark is 625 range and single-target. Level chart disagreed on four of seven rows; full layer was all-Skill against a content layer that matches packet.levelChart — fixed as one atomic group, and phases[4].why / phases[5].why were rewritten because they described Ahri power spikes on rows the chart gives to Zed.
